title: Input slice of an encoded snapshot
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet with $k$ work tapes, let a binary code of width $B$ be given for its optional states, and let $s$ be a snapshot of $M$. The two bits in the input-symbol slice of the encoded snapshot are exactly the two-bit encoding of the input symbol in $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite binary-alphabet machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes
A binary code of width $B$ for the optional states of $M$
replaced: For every snapshot $s$ of a machine with a fixed optional-state binary code, the input slice of the encoded block of $s$ equals the two-bit encoding of the input symbol of $s$.
